data.exact_reserve_text: The Property Treaty team was loss making following the above average natural catastrophe activity in 2022 despite benefitting from reductions in prior years' loss estimates. The EL/PL book was profitable in 2022; it continues to benefit from re-underwriting of the book implemented over the past few years and favourable loss activity in the year. The International Casualty and Motor books benefitted from favourable prior year development but they were adversely impacted by increases in the Annual Survey of Hours and Earnings (ASHE) due to heightened inflation in the UK. The syndicate has considered the expected movements in the UK Personal Injury Discount Rate and has reserved for these accordingly.
data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced an overall gross prior year reserve release of GBP 35.3 million, representing a 2.9% release of opening gross claims outstanding. This was primarily driven by favourable claims development across several lines of business, including Property Treaty, EL/PL, International Casualty, and Motor. The Property Treaty team benefited from reductions in prior years' loss estimates, while the EL/PL book saw favourable loss activity. International Casualty and Motor also experienced favourable prior year development, although these benefits were partially offset by adverse impacts from increases in the Annual Survey of Hours and Earnings (ASHE) due to heightened inflation in the UK. The syndicate also considered expected movements in the UK Personal Injury Discount Rate in its reserving.

Reserves established in recent years in respect of other natural catastrophe events have, in aggregate, proved to be adequate.
